system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Chicago, United States. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Chicago itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Chicago space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (West Town/West Loop, River North, Pilsen/Bridgeport, Logan Square/Wicker Park, Garfield Park, Hyde Park) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Chicago spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Chicago, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: GRAY
galleries.note: Chicago’s leading blue-chip gallery, with a formidable postwar and contemporary roster and sustained international fair and museum visibility.

galleries.name: Kavi Gupta
galleries.note: Globally active gallery known for ambitious exhibitions, major art-fair participation and an influential multicultural programme.

galleries.name: Mariane Ibrahim
galleries.note: Internationally prominent gallery championing artists of Africa and its diaspora, with spaces in Chicago, Paris and Mexico City.

galleries.name: The Renaissance Society
galleries.note: Historic non-collecting contemporary institution whose commissioned exhibitions and publications exert exceptional critical influence.

galleries.name: Corbett vs. Dempsey
galleries.note: Internationally respected for rigorous contemporary art, Chicago modernism, artist estates, experimental music and scholarship.

galleries.name: moniquemeloche
galleries.note: A major incubator of emerging and mid-career artists, with strong museum placements and international fair exposure.

galleries.name: PATRON
galleries.note: Highly regarded contemporary programme with a diverse roster and a visible presence at leading international fairs.

galleries.name: DOCUMENT
galleries.note: Conceptually focused gallery and publisher whose artists receive growing international institutional and critical attention.

galleries.name: The Arts Club of Chicago
galleries.note: Centuries-spanning membership institution with a distinguished record of presenting adventurous contemporary exhibitions and commissions.

galleries.name: Hyde Park Art Center
galleries.note: A foundational Chicago art center supporting experimentation, exhibitions, residencies and artist development across generations.

galleries.name: Anthony Gallery
galleries.note: Fast-rising gallery with a culturally resonant programme spanning contemporary art, design, music and Black creative communities.

galleries.name: Chicago Artists Coalition
galleries.note: Crucial artist-development institution whose residencies and exhibitions have launched numerous important Chicago careers.

galleries.name: Western Exhibitions
galleries.note: Long-running gallery recognized for idiosyncratic, materially inventive artists and a particularly strong commitment to works on paper.

galleries.name: Volume Gallery
galleries.note: Internationally influential platform at the intersection of contemporary art, collectible design, architecture and material experimentation.

galleries.name: Andrew Rafacz
galleries.note: Established contemporary gallery known for developing emerging artists and maintaining a consistent national fair presence.

galleries.name: Catherine Edelman Gallery
galleries.note: One of Chicago’s most important photography galleries, with decades of fair participation and institutional placements.

galleries.name: Graham Foundation
galleries.note: Globally influential architecture and visual-culture foundation presenting research-driven exhibitions, commissions and publications.

galleries.name: Goldfinch
galleries.note: Artist-founded gallery with a critically regarded programme linking Chicago practices to broader national conversations.

galleries.name: Wrightwood 659
galleries.note: Tadao Ando-designed exhibition space presenting ambitious art, architecture and socially engaged thematic projects.

galleries.name: Neubauer Collegium for Culture and Society
galleries.note: Research institute with a sophisticated exhibition programme built around major artists, scholars and original commissions.

galleries.name: Zolla/Lieberman Gallery
galleries.note: A durable River North gallery with a broad contemporary roster and more than four decades of Chicago influence.

galleries.name: Stony Island Arts Bank
galleries.note: Theaster Gates’s landmark Rebuild Foundation venue combines contemporary exhibitions, archives, performances and community cultural work.

galleries.name: Center for Native Futures
galleries.note: Native-led contemporary art center creating essential exhibition, research and professional opportunities for Indigenous artists.

galleries.name: Chicago Cultural Center
galleries.note: The city’s principal civic exhibition venue, mounting substantial free shows by Chicago and international contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Gallery 400
galleries.note: UIC’s critically engaged gallery, known for experimental exhibitions addressing social justice, politics and underrepresented histories.

galleries.name: Arts Incubator
galleries.note: University of Chicago Arts + Public Life hub supporting South Side artists through exhibitions, residencies and community programmes.

galleries.name: Thomas McCormick Gallery
galleries.note: Veteran gallery combining contemporary artists with significant postwar Chicago material and artist estates.

galleries.name: Co-Prosperity
galleries.note: Public Media Institute’s influential experimental venue for exhibitions, publishing, performance and artist-organized cultural projects.

galleries.name: South Side Community Art Center
galleries.note: Historic Black arts institution with an enduring role in contemporary exhibitions, education and Chicago cultural life.

galleries.name: Shane Campbell Gallery
galleries.note: Longstanding contemporary programme recognized for conceptually ambitious artists and sustained national critical attention.

galleries.name: FLXST Contemporary
galleries.note: Artist-run gallery foregrounding immigrant, diasporic and cross-cultural practices through exhibitions and curatorial collaborations.

galleries.name: Filter Photo
galleries.note: Important photography nonprofit presenting juried exhibitions, festivals, lectures and professional opportunities for lens-based artists.

galleries.name: ENGAGE Projects
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery emphasizing sustained artist relationships, thoughtful curation and accessible engagement with new work.

galleries.name: Devening Projects
galleries.note: Artist-led gallery and editions programme with a rigorous history of presenting Chicago, European and international practices.

galleries.name: M. LeBlanc
galleries.note: Closely watched emerging gallery noted for focused installations and a younger generation of conceptually driven artists.

galleries.name: Ruschman
galleries.note: Independent contemporary programme connecting Chicago artists with national and international collectors and curators.

galleries.name: Stephen Daiter Gallery
galleries.note: Respected specialist in modern and contemporary photography, particularly documentary, experimental and Chicago-centered work.

galleries.name: Regards
galleries.note: Artist-oriented contemporary gallery recognized for spare, challenging presentations and an adventurous emerging programme.

galleries.name: Mickey
galleries.note: Intimate gallery with a distinctive artist-driven programme and growing visibility beyond Chicago.

galleries.name: Sarai
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery building dialogue among Chicago-based and international artists through polished thematic and solo exhibitions.

galleries.name: Roman Susan
galleries.note: Artist-run nonprofit supporting experimental exhibitions, public projects and neighborhood-rooted cultural exchange.

galleries.name: Roots & Culture
galleries.note: Influential artist-run space that has introduced many emerging Chicago artists through exhibitions and residency programmes.

galleries.name: Heaven Gallery
galleries.note: Long-lived artist-run gallery central to Wicker Park’s independent art history and interdisciplinary creative community.

galleries.name: Tiger Strikes Asteroid Chicago
galleries.note: Chicago branch of the national artist-run network, facilitating exchanges and experimental group and solo exhibitions.

galleries.name: Woman Made Gallery
galleries.note: Longstanding feminist nonprofit dedicated to women and nonbinary artists through exhibitions, advocacy and public programmes.

galleries.name: 6018North
galleries.note: Socially engaged arts center presenting interdisciplinary exhibitions, performances and projects focused on civic dialogue.

galleries.name: Julius Caesar
galleries.note: Influential artist-run gallery known for emerging practices, collaborative experimentation and its role in Chicago’s alternative ecosystem.

galleries.name: Prairie
galleries.note: Closely watched artist-run space presenting concise, experimental exhibitions by local and visiting artists.

galleries.name: Good Weather
galleries.note: Permanent Chicago outpost of the artist-run project, bringing an inventive interstate network into the local scene.

galleries.name: Weatherproof
galleries.note: Independent exhibition space valued for experimental presentations and strong connections to younger artist communities.

galleries.name: Boundary
galleries.note: Storefront artist-run space presenting focused contemporary exhibitions in a neighborhood far from the main gallery districts.

galleries.name: LVL3
galleries.note: Artist-run platform with a long record of pairing emerging Chicago artists with national and international peers.

galleries.name: ARC Gallery
galleries.note: Pioneering women-founded cooperative gallery providing sustained exhibition opportunities and an enduring feminist legacy.

galleries.name: Vertical Gallery
galleries.note: Chicago’s leading commercial venue for urban, street-influenced and contemporary graphic art.

galleries.name: Blanc Gallery
galleries.note: Bronzeville venue presenting contemporary Black art, culturally focused exhibitions and community programming.

galleries.name: Gallery Guichard
galleries.note: Longstanding gallery specializing in art of the African diaspora and supporting Bronzeville’s cultural infrastructure.

galleries.name: Alan Koppel Gallery
galleries.note: Established dealer presenting blue-chip modern and contemporary art alongside selected emerging and mid-career work.

galleries.name: Addington Gallery
galleries.note: Durable River North gallery known for contemporary painting, sculpture and technically accomplished material practices.

galleries.name: Gruen Galleries
galleries.note: Long-running family gallery presenting contemporary American and international painting and sculpture.

galleries.name: Jean Albano Gallery
galleries.note: Veteran Chicago gallery with an eclectic contemporary roster and longstanding ties to local collectors and artists.

galleries.name: Bert Green Fine Art
galleries.note: Independent gallery and publisher presenting contemporary artists, works on paper and politically attentive projects.

galleries.name: Gallery Victor
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery with a broad programme spanning painting, photography, sculpture and internationally sourced work.

galleries.name: Povos
galleries.note: Emerging commercial gallery supporting accessible collecting and a diverse roster of younger contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Blue Gallery
galleries.note: Wicker Park gallery presenting contemporary painting, sculpture and multimedia work by Chicago and visiting artists.

galleries.name: Bendixen Contemporary
galleries.note: Independent gallery developing an international-leaning programme of emerging and established contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Galerie F
galleries.note: Prominent local platform for street art, printmaking, illustration and Chicago’s urban contemporary scene.

galleries.name: Chicago Truborn
galleries.note: Street-art-focused gallery providing sustained visibility for muralists, illustrators and self-taught contemporary artists.

galleries.name: ACRE Projects
galleries.note: Exhibition arm of ACRE’s artist residency, historically important for introducing experimental early-career work in Chicago.

galleries.name: Comfort Station
galleries.note: Tiny historic building transformed into a lively multidisciplinary venue for installations, screenings, sound and performance.

galleries.name: Elastic Arts
galleries.note: Artist-run interdisciplinary organization pairing visual exhibitions with one of Chicago’s strongest experimental music programmes.

galleries.name: Agitator Gallery
galleries.note: Cooperative gallery emphasizing politically engaged art, community debate and opportunities for underrepresented artists.

galleries.name: Spudnik Press Cooperative
galleries.note: Major community printmaking center with a public gallery devoted to contemporary print, book and paper practices.

galleries.name: Chicago Printmakers Collaborative
galleries.note: Long-established print studio and gallery exhibiting accomplished contemporary printmakers from Chicago and beyond.

galleries.name: Perspective Gallery
galleries.note: Photography cooperative with a consistent exhibition programme supporting fine-art and documentary image makers.

galleries.name: Circle Contemporary
galleries.note: Nonprofit gallery presenting Illinois artists and building links between contemporary practice and regional art history.

galleries.name: 4th Ward Project Space
galleries.note: Intimate artist-run venue contributing an independent experimental programme to the Hyde Park art community.

galleries.name: Slow
galleries.note: Long-running domestic project space known for modestly scaled, thoughtful exhibitions and artist-led conversation.

galleries.name: Chicago Art Department
galleries.note: Community-oriented arts organization offering galleries, studios and experimental programming in Pilsen.

galleries.name: Mana Contemporary Chicago
galleries.note: Large arts complex housing studios, collections and rotating contemporary exhibitions under one roof.

galleries.name: Zhou B Art Center

galleries.name: Bridgeport Art Center

galleries.name: Logan Center Exhibitions

galleries.name: Gray Center for Arts and Inquiry

galleries.name: PO Box Collective
galleries.note: Community-based artist collective presenting exhibitions, workshops and socially engaged programming in Rogers Park.

galleries.name: Iceberg Projects

galleries.name: The Franklin
galleries.note: Artist-built backyard pavilion with a longstanding experimental programme and an influential do-it-yourself ethos.

galleries.name: Four A.M.

galleries.name: No Nation Art Lab

galleries.name: Color Club

galleries.name: Rotofugi Gallery

galleries.name: Gallery19
galleries.note: Photography-focused gallery presenting contemporary fine-art image makers through solo and thematic exhibitions.

galleries.name: Elephant Room Gallery

galleries.name: Oliva Gallery
galleries.note: Neighborhood contemporary gallery with a varied programme of painting, sculpture, installation and community events.

galleries.name: The Martin
galleries.note: Artist-centered venue presenting exhibitions, performances and pop-up projects in an informal domestic-scale setting.

galleries.name: Pilsen Arts & Community House
galleries.note: Community cultural space giving artists and neighborhood groups an accessible platform for exhibitions and public programmes.

galleries.name: Belong Gallery
galleries.note: Community-minded gallery emphasizing inclusion, collaboration and accessible opportunities for emerging artists.

galleries.name: Epiphany Center for the Arts
galleries.note: Restored cultural complex whose visual-art programme complements extensive music, performance and interdisciplinary offerings.

galleries.name: Hairpin Arts Center

galleries.name: Segundo Ruiz Belvis Cultural Center

galleries.name: Soccer Club Club
